units.rightText: Twelve years they served Chedorlaomer, and in the thirteenth year they rebelled.

units.leftText: In the fourteenth year Chedorlaomer and the kings who were with him came and struck the Rephaim in Ashteroth Karnaim, the Zuzim in Ham, the Emim in Shaveh Kiriathaim,
units.rightText: And in the fourteenth year came Chedorlaomer, and the kings that were with him, and smote the Rephaim in Ashteroth-karnaim, and the Zuzim in Ham, and the Emim in Shaveh-kiriathaim,

units.leftText: and the Horites in their Mount Seir, to El Paran, which is by the wilderness.
units.rightText: and the Horites in their mount Seir, unto El-paran, which is by the wilderness.

units.leftText: They returned, and came to En Mishpat (also called Kadesh), and struck all the country of the Amalekites, and also the Amorites, that lived in Hazazon Tamar.
units.rightText: And they returned, and came to En-mishpat (the same is Kadesh), and smote all the country of the Amalekites, and also the Amorites, that dwelt in Hazazon-tamar.

units.leftText: The king of Sodom, and the king of Gomorrah, the king of Admah, the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (also called Zoar) went out; and they set the battle in array against them in the valley of Siddim
units.rightText: And there went out the king of Sodom, and the king of Gomorrah, and the king of Admah, and the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (the same is Zoar); and they set the battle in array against them in the vale of Siddim;

units.leftText: against Chedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of Goiim, Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar; four kings against the five.
units.rightText: against Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goiim, and Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar; four kings against the five.

units.leftText: Now the valley of Siddim was full of tar pits; and the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, and some fell there. Those who remained fled to the hills.
units.rightText: Now the vale of Siddim was full of slime pits; and the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, and they fell there, and they that remained fled to the mountain.

units.leftText: They took all the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah, and all their food, and went their way.
units.rightText: And they took all the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah, and all their victuals, and went their way.

units.leftText: They took Lot, Abram’s brother’s son, who lived in Sodom, and his goods, and departed.
units.rightText: And they took Lot, Abram’s brother’s son, who dwelt in Sodom, and his goods, and departed.

units.leftText: One who had escaped came and told Abram, the Hebrew. At that time, he lived by the oaks of Mamre, the Amorite, brother of Eshcol and brother of Aner. They were allies of Abram.
units.rightText: And there came one that had escaped, and told Abram the Hebrew: now he dwelt by the oaks of Mamre, the Amorite, brother of Eshcol, and brother of Aner; and these were confederate with Abram.

units.leftText: When Abram heard that his relative was taken captive, he led out his three hundred eighteen trained men, born in his house, and pursued as far as Dan.
units.rightText: And when Abram heard that his brother was taken captive, he led forth his trained men, born in his house, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued as far as Dan.

units.leftText: He divided himself against them by night, he and his servants, and struck them, and pursued them to Hobah, which is on the left hand of Damascus.
units.rightText: And he divided himself against them by night, he and his servants, and smote them, and pursued them unto Hobah, which is on the left hand of Damascus.

units.leftText: He brought back all the goods, and also brought back his relative Lot and his goods, and the women also, and the other people.
units.rightText: And he brought back all the goods, and also brought back his brother Lot, and his goods, and the women also, and the people.

units.leftText: The king of Sodom went out to meet him after his return from the slaughter of Chedorlaomer and the kings who were with him, at the valley of Shaveh (that is, the King’s Valley).
units.rightText: And the king of Sodom went out to meet him, after his return from the slaughter of Chedorlaomer and the kings that were with him, at the vale of Shaveh (the same is the King’s Vale).

units.leftText: Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine. He was priest of God Most High.
units.rightText: And Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine: and he was priest of God Most High.

units.leftText: He blessed him, and said, “Blessed be Abram of God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth.
units.rightText: And he blessed him, and said, Blessed be Abram of God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth:

units.leftText: Blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand.”
units.rightText: and blessed be God Most High, who hath delivered thine enemies into thy hand. And he gave him a tenth of all.

units.leftText: The king of Sodom said to Abram, “Give me the people, and take the goods for yourself.”
units.rightText: And the king of Sodom said unto Abram, Give me the persons, and take the goods to thyself.

units.leftText: Abram said to the king of Sodom, “I have lifted up my hand to the LORD, God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth,
units.rightText: And Abram said to the king of Sodom, I have lifted up my hand unto Jehovah, God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth,

units.leftText: that I will not take a thread nor a sandal strap nor anything that is yours, lest you should say, ‘I have made Abram rich.’
units.rightText: that I will not take a thread nor a shoe-latchet nor aught that is thine, lest thou shouldest say, I have made Abram rich:

units.leftText: I will accept nothing from you except that which the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who went with me: Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre. Let them take their portion.”
units.rightText: save only that which the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men that went with me, Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre; let them take their portion.

units.leftText: After these things the LORD’s word came to Abram in a vision, saying, “Don’t be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your exceedingly great reward.”
units.rightText: After these things the word of Jehovah came unto Abram in a vision, saying, Fear not, Abram: I am thy shield, and thy exceeding great reward.

units.leftText: Abram said, “Lord GOD, what will you give me, since I go childless, and he who will inherit my estate is Eliezer of Damascus?”
units.rightText: And Abram said, O Lord Jehovah, what wilt thou give me, seeing I go childless, and he that shall be possessor of my house is Eliezer of Damascus?

units.leftText: Abram said, “Behold, you have given no children to me: and, behold, one born in my house is my heir.”
units.rightText: And Abram said, Behold, to me thou hast given no seed: and, lo, one born in my house is mine heir.

units.leftText: Behold, the LORD’s word came to him, saying, “This man will not be your heir, but he who will come out of your own body will be your heir.”
units.rightText: And, behold, the word of Jehovah came unto him, saying, This man shall not be thine heir; but he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels shall be thine heir.

units.leftText: The LORD brought him outside, and said, “Look now toward the sky, and count the stars, if you are able to count them.” He said to Abram, “So your offspring will be.”
units.rightText: And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and number the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be.

units.leftText: He believed in the LORD, who credited it to him for righteousness.
units.rightText: And he believed in Jehovah; and he reckoned it to him for righteousness.

units.leftText: He said to Abram, “I am the LORD who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldees, to give you this land to inherit it.”
units.rightText: And he said unto him, I am Jehovah that brought thee out of Ur of the Chaldees, to give thee this land to inherit it.

units.leftText: He said, “Lord GOD, how will I know that I will inherit it?”
units.rightText: And he said, O Lord Jehovah, whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it?

units.leftText: He said to him, “Bring me a heifer three years old, a female goat three years old, a ram three years old, a turtledove, and a young pigeon.”
units.rightText: And he said unto him, Take me a heifer three years old, and a she-goat three years old, and a ram three years old, and a turtle-dove, and a young pigeon.

units.leftText: He brought him all these, and divided them in the middle, and laid each half opposite the other; but he didn’t divide the birds.
units.rightText: And he took him all these, and divided them in the midst, and laid each half over against the other: but the birds divided he not.

units.leftText: The birds of prey came down on the carcasses, and Abram drove them away.
units.rightText: And the birds of prey came down upon the carcasses, and Abram drove them away.

units.leftText: When the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell on Abram. Now terror and great darkness fell on him.
units.rightText: And when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and, lo, a horror of great darkness fell upon him.

units.leftText: He said to Abram, “Know for sure that your offspring will live as foreigners in a land that is not theirs, and will serve them. They will afflict them four hundred years.
units.rightText: And he said unto Abram, Know of a surety that thy seed shall be sojourners in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;

units.leftText: I will also judge that nation, whom they will serve. Afterward they will come out with great wealth;
units.rightText: and also that nation, whom they shall serve, will I judge: and afterward shall they come out with great substance.

units.leftText: but you will go to your fathers in peace. You will be buried at a good old age.
units.rightText: But thou shalt go to thy fathers in peace; thou shalt be buried in a good old age.

units.leftText: In the fourth generation they will come here again, for the iniquity of the Amorite is not yet full.”
units.rightText: And in the fourth generation they shall come hither again: for the iniquity of the Amorite is not yet full.

units.leftText: It came to pass that, when the sun went down, and it was dark, behold, a smoking furnace and a flaming torch passed between these pieces.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, that, when the sun went down, and it was dark, behold, a smoking furnace, and a flaming torch that passed between these pieces.

units.leftText: In that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying, “I have given this land to your offspring, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates:
units.rightText: In that day Jehovah made a covenant with Abram, saying, Unto thy seed have I given this land, from the river of Egypt unto the great river, the river Euphrates:

units.leftText: the land of the Kenites, the Kenizzites, the Kadmonites,
units.rightText: the Kenite, and the Kenizzite, and the Kadmonite,

units.leftText: the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Rephaim,
units.rightText: and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, and the Rephaim,

units.leftText: the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.”
units.rightText: and the Amorite, and the Canaanite, and the Girgashite, and the Jebusite.

units.leftText: Now Sarai, Abram’s wife, bore him no children. She had a servant, an Egyptian, whose name was Hagar.
units.rightText: Now Sarai, Abram’s wife, bare him no children: and she had a handmaid, an Egyptian, whose name was Hagar.

units.leftText: Sarai said to Abram, “See now, the LORD has restrained me from bearing. Please go in to my servant. It may be that I will obtain children by her.” Abram listened to the voice of Sarai.
units.rightText: And Sarai said unto Abram, Behold now, Jehovah hath restrained me from bearing; go in, I pray thee, unto my handmaid; it may be that I shall obtain children by her. And Abram hearkened to the voice of Sarai.

units.leftText: Sarai, Abram’s wife, took Hagar the Egyptian, her servant, after Abram had lived ten years in the land of Canaan, and gave her to Abram her husband to be his wife.
units.rightText: And Sarai, Abram’s wife, took Hagar the Egyptian, her handmaid, after Abram had dwelt ten years in the land of Canaan, and gave her to Abram her husband to be his wife.

units.leftText: He went in to Hagar, and she conceived. When she saw that she had conceived, her mistress was despised in her eyes.
units.rightText: And he went in unto Hagar, and she conceived: and when she saw that she had conceived, her mistress was despised in her eyes.

units.leftText: Sarai said to Abram, “This wrong is your fault. I gave my servant into your bosom, and when she saw that she had conceived, she despised me. May the LORD judge between me and you.”
units.rightText: And Sarai said unto Abram, My wrong be upon thee: I gave my handmaid into thy bosom; and when she saw that she had conceived, I was despised in her eyes: Jehovah judge between me and thee.

units.leftText: But Abram said to Sarai, “Behold, your maid is in your hand. Do to her whatever is good in your eyes.” Sarai dealt harshly with her, and she fled from her face.
units.rightText: But Abram said unto Sarai, Behold, thy maid is in thy hand; do to her that which is good in thine eyes. And Sarai dealt hardly with her, and she fled from her face.

units.leftText: The LORD’s angel found her by a fountain of water in the wilderness, by the fountain on the way to Shur.
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah found her by a fountain of water in the wilderness, by the fountain in the way to Shur.

units.leftText: He said, “Hagar, Sarai’s servant, where did you come from? Where are you going?”
units.rightText: And he said, Hagar, Sarai’s handmaid, whence camest thou? and whither goest thou? And she said, I am fleeing from the face of my mistress Sarai.

units.leftText: The LORD’s angel said to her, “Return to your mistress, and submit yourself under her hands.”
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah said unto her, Return to thy mistress, and submit thyself under her hands.

units.leftText: The LORD’s angel said to her, “I will greatly multiply your offspring, that they will not be counted for multitude.”
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah said unto her, I will greatly multiply thy seed, that it shall not be numbered for multitude.

units.leftText: The LORD’s angel said to her, “Behold, you are with child, and will bear a son. You shall call his name Ishmael, because the LORD has heard your affliction.
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah said unto her, Behold, thou art with child, and shalt bear a son; and thou shalt call his name Ishmael, because Jehovah hath heard thy affliction.

units.leftText: He will be like a wild donkey among men. His hand will be against every man, and every man’s hand against him. He will live opposed to all of his brothers.”
units.rightText: And he shall be as a wild ass among men; his hand shall be against every man, and every man’s hand against him; and he shall dwell over against all his brethren.

units.leftText: She called the name of the LORD who spoke to her, “You are a God who sees,” for she said, “Have I even stayed alive after seeing him?”
units.rightText: And she called the name of Jehovah that spake unto her, Thou art a God that seeth: for she said, Have I even here looked after him that seeth me?

units.leftText: Therefore the well was called Beer Lahai Roi. Behold, it is between Kadesh and Bered.
units.rightText: Wherefore the well was called Beer-lahai-roi; behold, it is between Kadesh and Bered.
leftNotes: 16:14 Beer Lahai Roi means “well of the one who lives and sees me”.

units.leftText: Hagar bore a son for Abram. Abram called the name of his son, whom Hagar bore, Ishmael.
units.rightText: And Hagar bare Abram a son: and Abram called the name of his son, whom Hagar bare, Ishmael.

units.leftText: Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram.
units.rightText: And Abram was fourscore and six years old, when Hagar bare Ishmael to Abram.

units.leftText: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the LORD appeared to Abram and said to him, “I am God Almighty. Walk before me and be blameless.
units.rightText: And when Abram was ninety years old and nine, Jehovah appeared to Abram, and said unto him, I am God Almighty; walk before me, and be thou perfect.

units.leftText: I will make my covenant between me and you, and will multiply you exceedingly.”
units.rightText: And I will make my covenant between me and thee, and will multiply thee exceedingly.

units.leftText: Abram fell on his face. God talked with him, saying,
units.rightText: And Abram fell on his face: and God talked with him, saying,

units.leftText: “As for me, behold, my covenant is with you. You will be the father of a multitude of nations.
units.rightText: As for me, behold, my covenant is with thee, and thou shalt be the father of a multitude of nations.

units.leftText: Your name will no more be called Abram, but your name will be Abraham; for I have made you the father of a multitude of nations.
units.rightText: Neither shall thy name any more be called Abram, but thy name shall be Abraham; for the father of a multitude of nations have I made thee.

units.leftText: I will make you exceedingly fruitful, and I will make nations of you. Kings will come out of you.
units.rightText: And I will make thee exceeding fruitful, and I will make nations of thee, and kings shall come out of thee.

units.leftText: I will establish my covenant between me and you and your offspring after you throughout their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a God to you and to your offspring after you.
units.rightText: And I will establish my covenant between me and thee and thy seed after thee throughout their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a God unto thee and to thy seed after thee.

units.leftText: I will give to you, and to your offspring after you, the land where you are traveling, all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession. I will be their God.”
units.rightText: And I will give unto thee, and to thy seed after thee, the land of thy sojournings, all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession; and I will be their God.

units.leftText: God said to Abraham, “As for you, you shall keep my covenant, you and your offspring after you throughout their generations.
units.rightText: And God said unto Abraham, And as for thee, thou shalt keep my covenant, thou, and thy seed after thee throughout their generations.

units.leftText: This is my covenant, which you shall keep, between me and you and your offspring after you. Every male among you shall be circumcised.
units.rightText: This is my covenant, which ye shall keep, between me and you and thy seed after thee: every male among you shall be circumcised.

units.leftText: You shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskin. It will be a token of the covenant between me and you.
units.rightText: And ye shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskin; and it shall be a token of a covenant betwixt me and you.

units.leftText: He who is eight days old shall be circumcised among you, every male throughout your generations, he who is born in the house, or bought with money from any foreigner who is not of your offspring.
units.rightText: And he that is eight days old shall be circumcised among you, every male throughout your generations, he that is born in the house, or bought with money of any foreigner that is not of thy seed.

units.leftText: He who is born in your house, and he who is bought with your money, must be circumcised. My covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant.
units.rightText: He that is born in thy house, and he that is bought with thy money, must needs be circumcised: and my covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant.

units.leftText: The uncircumcised male who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin, that soul shall be cut off from his people. He has broken my covenant.”
units.rightText: And the uncircumcised male who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin, that soul shall be cut off from his people; he hath broken my covenant.

units.leftText: God said to Abraham, “As for Sarai your wife, you shall not call her name Sarai, but her name shall be Sarah.
units.rightText: And God said unto Abraham, As for Sarai thy wife, thou shalt not call her name Sarai, but Sarah shall her name be.

units.leftText: I will bless her, and moreover I will give you a son by her. Yes, I will bless her, and she will be a mother of nations. Kings of peoples will come from her.”
units.rightText: And I will bless her, and moreover I will give thee a son of her: yea, I will bless her, and she shall be a mother of nations; kings of peoples shall be of her.

units.leftText: Then Abraham fell on his face, and laughed, and said in his heart, “Will a child be born to him who is one hundred years old? Will Sarah, who is ninety years old, give birth?”
units.rightText: Then Abraham fell upon his face, and laughed, and said in his heart, Shall a child be born unto him that is a hundred years old? and shall Sarah, that is ninety years old, bear?

units.leftText: Abraham said to God, “Oh that Ishmael might live before you!”
units.rightText: And Abraham said unto God, Oh that Ishmael might live before thee!

units.leftText: God said, “No, but Sarah, your wife, will bear you a son. You shall call his name Isaac. I will establish my covenant with him for an everlasting covenant for his offspring after him.
units.rightText: And God said, Nay, but Sarah thy wife shall bear thee a son; and thou shalt call his name Isaac: and I will establish my covenant with him for an everlasting covenant for his seed after him.

units.leftText: As for Ishmael, I have heard you. Behold, I have blessed him, and will make him fruitful, and will multiply him exceedingly. He will become the father of twelve princes, and I will make him a great nation.
units.rightText: And as for Ishmael, I have heard thee: behold, I have blessed him, and will make him fruitful, and will multiply him exceedingly; twelve princes shall he beget, and I will make him a great nation.

units.leftText: But I will establish my covenant with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you at this set time next year.”
units.rightText: But my covenant will I establish with Isaac, whom Sarah shall bear unto thee at this set time in the next year.

units.leftText: When he finished talking with him, God went up from Abraham.
units.rightText: And he left off talking with him, and God went up from Abraham.

units.leftText: Abraham took Ishmael his son, all who were born in his house, and all who were bought with his money: every male among the men of Abraham’s house, and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin in the same day, as God had said to him.
units.rightText: And Abraham took Ishmael his son, and all that were born in his house, and all that were bought with his money, every male among the men of Abraham’s house, and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin in the selfsame day, as God had said unto him.

units.leftText: Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
units.rightText: And Abraham was ninety years old and nine, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.

units.leftText: Ishmael, his son, was thirteen years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
units.rightText: And Ishmael his son was thirteen years old, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.

units.leftText: In the same day both Abraham and Ishmael, his son, were circumcised.
units.rightText: In the selfsame day was Abraham circumcised, and Ishmael his son.

units.leftText: All the men of his house, those born in the house, and those bought with money from a foreigner, were circumcised with him.
units.rightText: And all the men of his house, those born in the house, and those bought with money of a foreigner, were circumcised with him.

units.leftText: The LORD appeared to him by the oaks of Mamre, as he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day.
units.rightText: And Jehovah appeared unto him by the oaks of Mamre, as he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day;

units.leftText: He lifted up his eyes and looked, and saw that three men stood near him. When he saw them, he ran to meet them from the tent door, and bowed himself to the earth,
units.rightText: and he lifted up his eyes and looked, and, lo, three men stood over against him: and when he saw them, he ran to meet them from the tent door, and bowed himself to the earth,

units.leftText: and said, “My lord, if now I have found favor in your sight, please don’t go away from your servant.
units.rightText: and said, My lord, if now I have found favor in thy sight, pass not away, I pray thee, from thy servant:

units.leftText: Now let a little water be fetched, wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree.
units.rightText: let now a little water be fetched, and wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree:

units.leftText: I will get a piece of bread so you can refresh your heart. After that you may go your way, now that you have come to your servant.”
units.rightText: and I will fetch a morsel of bread, and strengthen ye your heart; after that ye shall pass on: forasmuch as ye are come to your servant. And they said, So do, as thou hast said.

units.leftText: Abraham hurried into the tent to Sarah, and said, “Quickly prepare three seahs of fine meal, knead it, and make cakes.”
units.rightText: And Abraham hastened into the tent unto Sarah, and said, Make ready quickly three measures of fine meal, knead it, and make cakes.
leftNotes: 18:6 1 seah is about 7 liters or 1.9 gallons or 0.8 pecks

units.leftText: Abraham ran to the herd, and fetched a tender and good calf, and gave it to the servant. He hurried to dress it.
units.rightText: And Abraham ran unto the herd, and fetched a calf tender and good, and gave it unto the servant; and he hasted to dress it.

units.leftText: He took butter, milk, and the calf which he had dressed, and set it before them. He stood by them under the tree, and they ate.
units.rightText: And he took butter, and milk, and the calf which he had dressed, and set it before them; and he stood by them under the tree, and they did eat.

units.leftText: They asked him, “Where is Sarah, your wife?”
units.rightText: And they said unto him, Where is Sarah thy wife? And he said, Behold, in the tent.

units.leftText: He said, “I will certainly return to you at about this time next year; and behold, Sarah your wife will have a son.”
units.rightText: And he said, I will certainly return unto thee when the season cometh round; and, lo, Sarah thy wife shall have a son. And Sarah heard in the tent door, which was behind him.

units.leftText: Now Abraham and Sarah were old, well advanced in age. Sarah had passed the age of childbearing.
units.rightText: Now Abraham and Sarah were old, and well stricken in age; it had ceased to be with Sarah after the manner of women.

units.leftText: Sarah laughed within herself, saying, “After I have grown old will I have pleasure, my lord being old also?”
units.rightText: And Sarah laughed within herself, saying, After I am waxed old shall I have pleasure, my lord being old also?

units.leftText: The LORD said to Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh, saying, ‘Will I really bear a child when I am old?’
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Abraham, Wherefore did Sarah laugh, saying, Shall I of a surety bear a child, who am old?

units.leftText: Is anything too hard for the LORD? At the set time I will return to you, when the season comes around, and Sarah will have a son.”
units.rightText: Is anything too hard for Jehovah? At the set time I will return unto thee, when the season cometh round, and Sarah shall have a son.

units.leftText: Then Sarah denied it, saying, “I didn’t laugh,” for she was afraid.
units.rightText: Then Sarah denied, saying, I laughed not; for she was afraid. And he said, Nay; but thou didst laugh.

units.leftText: The men rose up from there, and looked toward Sodom. Abraham went with them to see them on their way.
units.rightText: And the men rose up from thence, and looked toward Sodom: and Abraham went with them to bring them on the way.

units.leftText: The LORD said, “Will I hide from Abraham what I do,
units.rightText: And Jehovah said, Shall I hide from Abraham that which I do;

units.leftText: since Abraham will surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth will be blessed in him?
units.rightText: seeing that Abraham shall surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him?

units.leftText: For I have known him, to the end that he may command his children and his household after him, that they may keep the way of the LORD, to do righteousness and justice; to the end that the LORD may bring on Abraham that which he has spoken of him.”
units.rightText: For I have known him, to the end that he may command his children and his household after him, that they may keep the way of Jehovah, to do righteousness and justice; to the end that Jehovah may bring upon Abraham that which he hath spoken of him.

units.leftText: The LORD said, “Because the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and because their sin is very grievous,
units.rightText: And Jehovah said, Because the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and because their sin is very grievous;

units.leftText: I will go down now, and see whether their deeds are as bad as the reports which have come to me. If not, I will know.”

units.leftText: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba, and there he called on the name of the LORD, the Everlasting God.
units.rightText: And Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beer-sheba, and called there on the name of Jehovah, the Everlasting God.
leftNotes: 21:33 LORD or GOD in all caps is from the Hebrew יהוה Yahweh except when otherwise noted as being from the short form יה Yah.

units.leftText: Abraham lived as a foreigner in the land of the Philistines many days.
units.rightText: And Abraham sojourned in the land of the Philistines many days.

units.leftText: After these things, God tested Abraham, and said to him, “Abraham!”
units.rightText: And it came to pass after these things, that God did prove Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham; and he said, Here am I.

units.leftText: He said, “Now take your son, your only son, Isaac, whom you love, and go into the land of Moriah. Offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains which I will tell you of.”
units.rightText: And he said, Take now thy son, thine only son, whom thou lovest, even Isaac, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt-offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of.

units.leftText: Abraham rose early in the morning, and saddled his donkey; and took two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son. He split the wood for the burnt offering, and rose up, and went to the place of which God had told him.
units.rightText: And Abraham rose early in the morning, and saddled his ass, and took two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son; and he clave the wood for the burnt-offering, and rose up, and went unto the place of which God had told him.

units.leftText: On the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes, and saw the place far off.
units.rightText: On the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes, and saw the place afar off.

units.leftText: Abraham said to his young men, “Stay here with the donkey. The boy and I will go over there. We will worship, and come back to you.”
units.rightText: And Abraham said unto his young men, Abide ye here with the ass, and I and the lad will go yonder; and we will worship, and come again to you.

units.leftText: Abraham took the wood of the burnt offering and laid it on Isaac his son. He took in his hand the fire and the knife. They both went together.
units.rightText: And Abraham took the wood of the burnt-offering, and laid it upon Isaac his son; and he took in his hand the fire and the knife; and they went both of them together.

units.leftText: Isaac spoke to Abraham his father, and said, “My father?”
units.rightText: And Isaac spake unto Abraham his father, and said, My father: and he said, Here am I, my son. And he said, Behold, the fire and the wood: but where is the lamb for a burnt-offering?

units.leftText: Abraham said, “God will provide himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” So they both went together.
units.rightText: And Abraham said, God will provide himself the lamb for a burnt-offering, my son: so they went both of them together.

units.leftText: They came to the place which God had told him of. Abraham built the altar there, and laid the wood in order, bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar, on the wood.
units.rightText: And they came to the place which God had told him of; and Abraham built the altar there, and laid the wood in order, and bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar, upon the wood.

units.leftText: Abraham stretched out his hand, and took the knife to kill his son.
units.rightText: And Abraham stretched forth his hand, and took the knife to slay his son.

units.leftText: The LORD’s angel called to him out of the sky, and said, “Abraham, Abraham!”
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah called unto him out of heaven, and said, Abraham, Abraham: and he said, Here am I.

units.leftText: He said, “Don’t lay your hand on the boy or do anything to him. For now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me.”
units.rightText: And he said, Lay not thy hand upon the lad, neither do thou anything unto him; for now I know that thou fearest God, seeing thou hast not withheld thy son, thine only son, from me.

units.leftText: Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and saw that behind him was a ram caught in the thicket by his horns. Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering instead of his son.
units.rightText: And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, behind him a ram caught in the thicket by his horns: and Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt-offering in the stead of his son.

units.leftText: Abraham called the name of that place “The LORD Will Provide”. As it is said to this day, “On the LORD’s mountain, it will be provided.”
units.rightText: And Abraham called the name of that place Jehovah-jireh: as it is said to this day, In the mount of Jehovah it shall be provided.
leftNotes: 22:14 or, the LORD Jireh, or, the LORD Seeing

units.leftText: The LORD’s angel called to Abraham a second time out of the sky,
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah called unto Abraham a second time out of heaven,

units.leftText: and said, “‘I have sworn by myself,’ says the LORD, ‘because you have done this thing, and have not withheld your son, your only son,
units.rightText: and said, By myself have I sworn, saith Jehovah, because thou hast done this thing, and hast not withheld thy son, thine only son,

units.leftText: that I will bless you greatly, and I will multiply your offspring greatly like the stars of the heavens, and like the sand which is on the seashore. Your offspring will possess the gate of his enemies.
units.rightText: that in blessing I will bless thee, and in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heavens, and as the sand which is upon the sea-shore; and thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies;

units.leftText: All the nations of the earth will be blessed by your offspring, because you have obeyed my voice.’”
units.rightText: and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed; because thou hast obeyed my voice.

units.leftText: So Abraham returned to his young men, and they rose up and went together to Beersheba. Abraham lived at Beersheba.
units.rightText: So Abraham returned unto his young men, and they rose up and went together to Beer-sheba; and Abraham dwelt at Beer-sheba.

units.leftText: After these things, Abraham was told, “Behold, Milcah, she also has borne children to your brother Nahor:
units.rightText: And it came to pass after these things, that it was told Abraham, saying, Behold, Milcah, she also hath borne children unto thy brother Nahor:

units.leftText: Uz his firstborn, Buz his brother, Kemuel the father of Aram,
units.rightText: Uz his first-born, and Buz his brother, and Kemuel the father of Aram,

units.leftText: Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.”
units.rightText: and Chesed, and Hazo, and Pildash, and Jidlaph, and Bethuel.

units.leftText: Bethuel became the father of Rebekah. These eight Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham’s brother.
units.rightText: And Bethuel begat Rebekah: these eight did Milcah bear to Nahor, Abraham’s brother.

units.leftText: His concubine, whose name was Reumah, also bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.
units.rightText: And his concubine, whose name was Reumah, she also bare Tebah, and Gaham, and Tahash, and Maacah.

units.leftText: Sarah lived one hundred twenty-seven years. This was the length of Sarah’s life.
units.rightText: And the life of Sarah was a hundred and seven and twenty years: these were the years of the life of Sarah.

units.leftText: Sarah died in Kiriath Arba (also called Hebron), in the land of Canaan. Abraham came to mourn for Sarah, and to weep for her.
units.rightText: And Sarah died in Kiriath-arba (the same is Hebron), in the land of Canaan: and Abraham came to mourn for Sarah, and to weep for her.

units.leftText: Abraham rose up from before his dead and spoke to the children of Heth, saying,
units.rightText: And Abraham rose up from before his dead, and spake unto the children of Heth, saying,

units.leftText: “I am a stranger and a foreigner living with you. Give me a possession of a burying-place with you, that I may bury my dead out of my sight.”
units.rightText: I am a stranger and a sojourner with you: give me a possession of a burying-place with you, that I may bury my dead out of my sight.

units.leftText: The children of Heth answered Abraham, saying to him,
units.rightText: And the children of Heth answered Abraham, saying unto him,

units.leftText: “Hear us, my lord. You are a prince of God among us. Bury your dead in the best of our tombs. None of us will withhold from you his tomb. Bury your dead.”
units.rightText: Hear us, my lord; thou art a prince of God among us: in the choice of our sepulchres bury thy dead; none of us shall withhold from thee his sepulchre, but that thou mayest bury thy dead.

units.leftText: Abraham rose up, and bowed himself to the people of the land, to the children of Heth.
units.rightText: And Abraham rose up, and bowed himself to the people of the land, even to the children of Heth.

units.leftText: He talked with them, saying, “If you agree that I should bury my dead out of my sight, hear me, and entreat for me to Ephron the son of Zohar,
units.rightText: And he communed with them, saying, If it be your mind that I should bury my dead out of my sight, hear me, and entreat for me to Ephron the son of Zohar,

units.leftText: that he may sell me the cave of Machpelah, which he has, which is in the end of his field. For the full price let him sell it to me among you as a possession for a burial place.”
units.rightText: that he may give me the cave of Machpelah, which he hath, which is in the end of his field; for the full price let him give it to me in the midst of you for a possession of a burying-place.

units.leftText: Now Ephron was sitting in the middle of the children of Heth. Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the hearing of the children of Heth, even of all who went in at the gate of his city, saying,
units.rightText: Now Ephron was sitting in the midst of the children of Heth: and Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the audience of the children of Heth, even of all that went in at the gate of his city, saying,

units.leftText: “No, my lord, hear me. I give you the field, and I give you the cave that is in it. In the presence of the children of my people I give it to you. Bury your dead.”
units.rightText: Nay, my lord, hear me: the field give I thee, and the cave that is therein, I give it thee; in the presence of the children of my people give I it thee: bury thy dead.

units.leftText: Abraham bowed himself down before the people of the land.
units.rightText: And Abraham bowed himself down before the people of the land.

units.leftText: He spoke to Ephron in the audience of the people of the land, saying, “But if you will, please hear me. I will give the price of the field. Take it from me, and I will bury my dead there.”
units.rightText: And he spake unto Ephron in the audience of the people of the land, saying, But if thou wilt, I pray thee, hear me: I will give the price of the field; take it of me, and I will bury my dead there.

units.leftText: Ephron answered Abraham, saying to him,
units.rightText: And Ephron answered Abraham, saying unto him,

units.leftText: “My lord, listen to me. What is a piece of land worth four hundred shekels of silver between me and you? Therefore bury your dead.”
units.rightText: My lord, hearken unto me: a piece of land worth four hundred shekels of silver, what is that betwixt me and thee? bury therefore thy dead.
leftNotes: 23:15 A shekel is about 10 grams, so 400 shekels would be about 4 kg. or 8.8 pounds.

units.leftText: Abraham listened to Ephron. Abraham weighed to Ephron the silver which he had named in the hearing of the children of Heth, four hundred shekels of silver, according to the current merchants’ standard.
units.rightText: And Abraham hearkened unto Ephron; and Abraham weighed to Ephron the silver which he had named in the audience of the children of Heth, four hundred shekels of silver, current money with the merchant.

units.leftText: So the field of Ephron, which was in Machpelah, which was before Mamre, the field, the cave which was in it, and all the trees that were in the field, that were in all of its borders, were deeded
units.rightText: So the field of Ephron, which was in Machpelah, which was before Mamre, the field, and the cave which was therein, and all the trees that were in the field, that were in all the border thereof round about, were made sure

units.leftText: to Abraham for a possession in the presence of the children of Heth, before all who went in at the gate of his city.
units.rightText: unto Abraham for a possession in the presence of the children of Heth, before all that went in at the gate of his city.

units.leftText: After this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre (that is, Hebron), in the land of Canaan.
units.rightText: And after this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre (the same is Hebron), in the land of Canaan.

units.leftText: The field, and the cave that is in it, were deeded to Abraham by the children of Heth as a possession for a burial place.
units.rightText: And the field, and the cave that is therein, were made sure unto Abraham for a possession of a burying-place by the children of Heth.

units.leftText: Abraham was old, and well advanced in age. The LORD had blessed Abraham in all things.
units.rightText: And Abraham was old, and well stricken in age: and Jehovah had blessed Abraham in all things.

units.leftText: Abraham said to his servant, the elder of his house, who ruled over all that he had, “Please put your hand under my thigh.
units.rightText: And Abraham said unto his servant, the elder of his house, that ruled over all that he had, Put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh:

units.leftText: I will make you swear by the LORD, the God of heaven and the God of the earth, that you shall not take a wife for my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I live.
units.rightText: and I will make thee swear by Jehovah, the God of heaven and the God of the earth, that thou wilt not take a wife for my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell:

units.leftText: But you shall go to my country, and to my relatives, and take a wife for my son Isaac.”
units.rightText: but thou shalt go unto my country, and to my kindred, and take a wife for my son Isaac.

units.leftText: The servant said to him, “What if the woman isn’t willing to follow me to this land? Must I bring your son again to the land you came from?”
units.rightText: And the servant said unto him, Peradventure the woman will not be willing to follow me unto this land: must I needs bring thy son again unto the land from whence thou camest?

units.leftText: Abraham said to him, “Beware that you don’t bring my son there again.
units.rightText: And Abraham said unto him, Beware thou that thou bring not my son thither again.

units.leftText: The LORD, the God of heaven—who took me from my father’s house, and from the land of my birth, who spoke to me, and who swore to me, saying, ‘I will give this land to your offspring—he will send his angel before you, and you shall take a wife for my son from there.
units.rightText: Jehovah, the God of heaven, who took me from my father’s house, and from the land of my nativity, and who spake unto me, and who sware unto me, saying, Unto thy seed will I give this land; he will send his angel before thee, and thou shalt take a wife for my son from thence.

units.leftText: If the woman isn’t willing to follow you, then you shall be clear from this oath to me. Only you shall not bring my son there again.”
units.rightText: And if the woman be not willing to follow thee, then thou shalt be clear from this my oath; only thou shalt not bring my son thither again.

units.leftText: The servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master, and swore to him concerning this matter.
units.rightText: And the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master, and sware to him concerning this matter.

units.leftText: The servant took ten of his master’s camels, and departed, having a variety of good things of his master’s with him. He arose, and went to Mesopotamia, to the city of Nahor.
units.rightText: And the servant took ten camels, of the camels of his master, and departed, having all goodly things of his master’s in his hand: and he arose, and went to Mesopotamia, unto the city of Nahor.

units.leftText: He made the camels kneel down outside the city by the well of water at the time of evening, the time that women go out to draw water.
units.rightText: And he made the camels to kneel down without the city by the well of water at the time of evening, the time that women go out to draw water.

units.leftText: He said, “LORD, the God of my master Abraham, please give me success today, and show kindness to my master Abraham.
units.rightText: And he said, O Jehovah, the God of my master Abraham, send me, I pray thee, good speed this day, and show kindness unto my master Abraham.

units.leftText: Behold, I am standing by the spring of water. The daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water.
units.rightText: Behold, I am standing by the fountain of water; and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water:

units.leftText: Let it happen, that the young lady to whom I will say, ‘Please let down your pitcher, that I may drink,’ then she says, ‘Drink, and I will also give your camels a drink,’—let her be the one you have appointed for your servant Isaac. By this I will know that you have shown kindness to my master.”
units.rightText: and let it come to pass, that the damsel to whom I shall say, Let down thy pitcher, I pray thee, that I may drink; and she shall say, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: let the same be she that thou hast appointed for thy servant Isaac; and thereby shall I know that thou hast showed kindness unto my master.

units.leftText: Before he had finished speaking, behold, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel the son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, with her pitcher on her shoulder.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, before he had done speaking, that, behold, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel the son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, with her pitcher upon her shoulder.

units.leftText: The young lady was very beautiful to look at, a virgin. No man had known her. She went down to the spring, filled her pitcher, and came up.
units.rightText: And the damsel was very fair to look upon, a virgin, neither had any man known her: and she went down to the fountain, and filled her pitcher, and came up.

units.leftText: The servant ran to meet her, and said, “Please give me a drink, a little water from your pitcher.”
units.rightText: And the servant ran to meet her, and said, Give me to drink, I pray thee, a little water from thy pitcher.

units.leftText: She said, “Drink, my lord.” She hurried, and let down her pitcher on her hand, and gave him a drink.
units.rightText: And she said, Drink, my lord: and she hasted, and let down her pitcher upon her hand, and gave him drink.

units.leftText: When she had finished giving him a drink, she said, “I will also draw for your camels, until they have finished drinking.”
units.rightText: And when she had done giving him drink, she said, I will draw for thy camels also, until they have done drinking.

units.leftText: She hurried, and emptied her pitcher into the trough, and ran again to the well to draw, and drew for all his camels.
units.rightText: And she hasted, and emptied her pitcher into the trough, and ran again unto the well to draw, and drew for all his camels.

units.leftText: The man looked steadfastly at her, remaining silent, to know whether the LORD had made his journey prosperous or not.
units.rightText: And the man looked stedfastly on her, holding his peace, to know whether Jehovah had made his journey prosperous or not.

units.leftText: As the camels had finished drinking, the man took a golden ring of half a shekel weight, and two bracelets for her hands of ten shekels weight of gold,
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as the camels had done drinking, that the man took a golden ring of half a shekel weight, and two bracelets for her hands of ten shekels weight of gold,
leftNotes: 24:22 A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces.

units.leftText: and said, “Whose daughter are you? Please tell me. Is there room in your father’s house for us to stay?”
units.rightText: and said, Whose daughter art thou? tell me, I pray thee. Is there room in thy father’s house for us to lodge in?

units.leftText: She said to him, “I am the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, whom she bore to Nahor.”
units.rightText: And she said unto him, I am the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, whom she bare unto Nahor.

units.leftText: She said moreover to him, “We have both straw and feed enough, and room to lodge in.”
units.rightText: She said moreover unto him, We have both straw and provender enough, and room to lodge in.

units.leftText: The man bowed his head, and worshiped the LORD.
units.rightText: And the man bowed his head, and worshipped Jehovah.

units.leftText: He said, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who has not forsaken his loving kindness and his truth toward my master. As for me, the LORD has led me on the way to the house of my master’s relatives.”
units.rightText: And he said, Blessed be Jehovah, the God of my master Abraham, who hath not forsaken his lovingkindness and his truth toward my master: as for me, Jehovah hath led me in the way to the house of my master’s brethren.

units.leftText: The young lady ran, and told her mother’s house about these words.
units.rightText: And the damsel ran, and told her mother’s house according to these words.

units.leftText: Rebekah had a brother, and his name was Laban. Laban ran out to the man, to the spring.
units.rightText: And Rebekah had a brother, and his name was Laban: and Laban ran out unto the man, unto the fountain.

units.leftText: When he saw the ring, and the bracelets on his sister’s hands, and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister, saying, “This is what the man said to me,” he came to the man. Behold, he was standing by the camels at the spring.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when he saw the ring, and the bracelets upon his sister’s hands, and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister, saying, Thus spake the man unto me; that he came unto the man; and, behold, he was standing by the camels at the fountain.

units.leftText: He said, “Come in, you blessed of the LORD. Why do you stand outside? For I have prepared the house, and room for the camels.”
units.rightText: And he said, Come in, thou blessed of Jehovah; wherefore standest thou without? for I have prepared the house, and room for the camels.

units.leftText: The man came into the house, and he unloaded the camels. He gave straw and feed for the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him.
units.rightText: And the man came into the house, and he ungirded the camels; and he gave straw and provender for the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men that were with him.

units.leftText: Food was set before him to eat, but he said, “I will not eat until I have told my message.”
units.rightText: And there was set food before him to eat: but he said, I will not eat, until I have told mine errand. And he said, Speak on.

units.leftText: He said, “I am Abraham’s servant.
units.rightText: And he said, I am Abraham’s servant.

units.leftText: The LORD has blessed my master greatly. He has become great. The LORD has given him flocks and herds, silver and gold, male servants and female servants, and camels and donkeys.
units.rightText: And Jehovah hath blessed my master greatly; and he is become great: and he hath given him flocks and herds, and silver and gold, and men-servants and maid-servants, and camels and asses.

units.leftText: Sarah, my master’s wife, bore a son to my master when she was old. He has given all that he has to him.
units.rightText: And Sarah my master’s wife bare a son to my master when she was old: and unto him hath he given all that he hath.

units.leftText: My master made me swear, saying, ‘You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I live,
units.rightText: And my master made me swear, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife for my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I dwell:

units.leftText: but you shall go to my father’s house, and to my relatives, and take a wife for my son.’
units.rightText: but thou shalt go unto my father’s house, and to my kindred, and take a wife for my son.

units.leftText: I asked my master, ‘What if the woman will not follow me?’
units.rightText: And I said unto my master, Peradventure the woman will not follow me.

units.leftText: He said to me, ‘The LORD, before whom I walk, will send his angel with you, and prosper your way. You shall take a wife for my son from my relatives, and of my father’s house.
units.rightText: And he said unto me, Jehovah, before whom I walk, will send his angel with thee, and prosper thy way; and thou shalt take a wife for my son of my kindred, and of my father’s house:

units.leftText: Then you will be clear from my oath, when you come to my relatives. If they don’t give her to you, you shall be clear from my oath.’
units.rightText: then shalt thou be clear from my oath, when thou comest to my kindred; and if they give her not to thee, thou shalt be clear from my oath.

units.leftText: I came today to the spring, and said, ‘The LORD, the God of my master Abraham, if now you do prosper my way which I go—
units.rightText: And I came this day unto the fountain, and said, O Jehovah, the God of my master Abraham, if now thou do prosper my way which I go:

units.leftText: behold, I am standing by this spring of water. Let it happen, that the maiden who comes out to draw, to whom I will say, “Please give me a little water from your pitcher to drink,”
units.rightText: behold, I am standing by the fountain of water; and let it come to pass, that the maiden that cometh forth to draw, to whom I shall say, Give me, I pray thee, a little water from thy pitcher to drink;

units.leftText: then she tells me, “Drink, and I will also draw for your camels,”—let her be the woman whom the LORD has appointed for my master’s son.’
units.rightText: and she shall say to me, Both drink thou, and I will also draw for thy camels: let the same be the woman whom Jehovah hath appointed for my master’s son.

units.leftText: Before I had finished speaking in my heart, behold, Rebekah came out with her pitcher on her shoulder. She went down to the spring, and drew. I said to her, ‘Please let me drink.’
units.rightText: And before I had done speaking in my heart, behold, Rebekah came forth with her pitcher on her shoulder; and she went down unto the fountain, and drew: and I said unto her, Let me drink, I pray thee.

units.leftText: She hurried and let down her pitcher from her shoulder, and said, ‘Drink, and I will also give your camels a drink.’ So I drank, and she also gave the camels a drink.
units.rightText: And she made haste, and let down her pitcher from her shoulder, and said, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: so I drank, and she made the camels drink also.

units.leftText: I asked her, and said, ‘Whose daughter are you?’ She said, ‘The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor’s son, whom Milcah bore to him.’ I put the ring on her nose, and the bracelets on her hands.
units.rightText: And I asked her, and said, Whose daughter art thou? And she said, The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor’s son, whom Milcah bare unto him: and I put the ring upon her nose, and the bracelets upon her hands.

units.leftText: I bowed my head, and worshiped the LORD, and blessed the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who had led me in the right way to take my master’s brother’s daughter for his son.
units.rightText: And I bowed my head, and worshipped Jehovah, and blessed Jehovah, the God of my master Abraham, who had led me in the right way to take my master’s brother’s daughter for his son.

units.leftText: Now if you will deal kindly and truly with my master, tell me. If not, tell me, that I may turn to the right hand, or to the left.”
units.rightText: And now if ye will deal kindly and truly with my master, tell me: and if not, tell me; that I may turn to the right hand, or to the left.

units.leftText: Then Laban and Bethuel answered, “The thing proceeds from the LORD. We can’t speak to you bad or good.
units.rightText: Then Laban and Bethuel answered and said, The thing proceedeth from Jehovah: we cannot speak unto thee bad or good.

units.leftText: Behold, Rebekah is before you. Take her, and go, and let her be your master’s son’s wife, as the LORD has spoken.”
units.rightText: Behold, Rebekah is before thee, take her, and go, and let her be thy master’s son’s wife, as Jehovah hath spoken.

units.leftText: When Abraham’s servant heard their words, he bowed himself down to the earth to the LORD.

units.leftText: Leah also and her children came near, and bowed themselves. After them, Joseph came near with Rachel, and they bowed themselves.
units.rightText: And Leah also and her children came near, and bowed themselves: and after came Joseph near and Rachel, and they bowed themselves.

units.leftText: Esau said, “What do you mean by all this company which I met?”
units.rightText: And he said, What meanest thou by all this company which I met? And he said, To find favor in the sight of my lord.

units.leftText: Esau said, “I have enough, my brother; let that which you have be yours.”
units.rightText: And Esau said, I have enough, my brother; let that which thou hast be thine.

units.leftText: Jacob said, “Please, no, if I have now found favor in your sight, then receive my present at my hand, because I have seen your face, as one sees the face of God, and you were pleased with me.
units.rightText: And Jacob said, Nay, I pray thee, if now I have found favor in thy sight, then receive my present at my hand; forasmuch as I have seen thy face, as one seeth the face of God, and thou wast pleased with me.

units.leftText: Please take the gift that I brought to you, because God has dealt graciously with me, and because I have enough.” He urged him, and he took it.
units.rightText: Take, I pray thee, my gift that is brought to thee; because God hath dealt graciously with me, and because I have enough. And he urged him, and he took it.

units.leftText: Esau said, “Let’s take our journey, and let’s go, and I will go before you.”
units.rightText: And he said, Let us take our journey, and let us go, and I will go before thee.

units.leftText: Jacob said to him, “My lord knows that the children are tender, and that the flocks and herds with me have their young, and if they overdrive them one day, all the flocks will die.
units.rightText: And he said unto him, My lord knoweth that the children are tender, and that the flocks and herds with me have their young: and if they overdrive them one day, all the flocks will die.

units.leftText: Please let my lord pass over before his servant, and I will lead on gently, according to the pace of the livestock that are before me and according to the pace of the children, until I come to my lord to Seir.”
units.rightText: Let my lord, I pray thee, pass over before his servant: and I will lead on gently, according to the pace of the cattle that are before me and according to the pace of the children, until I come unto my lord unto Seir.

units.leftText: Esau said, “Let me now leave with you some of the people who are with me.”
units.rightText: And Esau said, Let me now leave with thee some of the folk that are with me. And he said, What needeth it? let me find favor in the sight of my lord.

units.leftText: So Esau returned that day on his way to Seir.
units.rightText: So Esau returned that day on his way unto Seir.

units.leftText: Jacob traveled to Succoth, built himself a house, and made shelters for his livestock. Therefore the name of the place is called Succoth.
units.rightText: And Jacob journeyed to Succoth, and built him a house, and made booths for his cattle: therefore the name of the place is called Succoth.

units.leftText: Jacob came in peace to the city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Paddan Aram; and encamped before the city.
units.rightText: And Jacob came in peace to the city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Paddan-aram; and encamped before the city.

units.leftText: He bought the parcel of ground where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for one hundred pieces of money.
units.rightText: And he bought the parcel of ground, where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for a hundred pieces of money.

units.leftText: He erected an altar there, and called it El Elohe Israel.
units.rightText: And he erected there an altar, and called it El-Elohe-Israel.

units.leftText: Dinah, the daughter of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.
units.rightText: And Dinah the daughter of Leah, whom she bare unto Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.

units.leftText: Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the land, saw her. He took her, lay with her, and humbled her.
units.rightText: And Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the land, saw her; and he took her, and lay with her, and humbled her.

units.leftText: His soul joined to Dinah, the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the young lady, and spoke kindly to the young lady.
units.rightText: And his soul clave unto Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the damsel, and spake kindly unto the damsel.

units.leftText: Shechem spoke to his father, Hamor, saying, “Get me this young lady as a wife.”
units.rightText: And Shechem spake unto his father Hamor, saying, Get me this damsel to wife.

units.leftText: Now Jacob heard that he had defiled Dinah, his daughter; and his sons were with his livestock in the field. Jacob held his peace until they came.
units.rightText: Now Jacob heard that he had defiled Dinah his daughter; and his sons were with his cattle in the field: and Jacob held his peace until they came.

units.leftText: Hamor the father of Shechem went out to Jacob to talk with him.
units.rightText: And Hamor the father of Shechem went out unto Jacob to commune with him.

units.leftText: The sons of Jacob came in from the field when they heard it. The men were grieved, and they were very angry, because he had done folly in Israel in lying with Jacob’s daughter, a thing that ought not to be done.
units.rightText: And the sons of Jacob came in from the field when they heard it: and the men were grieved, and they were very wroth, because he had wrought folly in Israel in lying with Jacob’s daughter; which thing ought not to be done.

units.leftText: Hamor talked with them, saying, “The soul of my son, Shechem, longs for your daughter. Please give her to him as a wife.
units.rightText: And Hamor communed with them, saying, The soul of my son Shechem longeth for your daughter: I pray you, give her unto him to wife.

units.leftText: Make marriages with us. Give your daughters to us, and take our daughters for yourselves.
units.rightText: And make ye marriages with us; give your daughters unto us, and take our daughters unto you.

units.leftText: You shall dwell with us, and the land will be before you. Live and trade in it, and get possessions in it.”
units.rightText: And ye shall dwell with us: and the land shall be before you; dwell and trade ye therein, and get you possessions therein.

units.leftText: Shechem said to her father and to her brothers, “Let me find favor in your eyes, and whatever you will tell me I will give.
units.rightText: And Shechem said unto her father and unto her brethren, Let me find favor in your eyes, and what ye shall say unto me I will give.

units.leftText: Ask me a great amount for a dowry, and I will give whatever you ask of me, but give me the young lady as a wife.”
units.rightText: Ask me never so much dowry and gift, and I will give according as ye shall say unto me: but give me the damsel to wife.

units.leftText: The sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father with deceit when they spoke, because he had defiled Dinah their sister,
units.rightText: And the sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father with guile, and spake, because he had defiled Dinah their sister,

units.leftText: and said to them, “We can’t do this thing, to give our sister to one who is uncircumcised; for that is a reproach to us.
units.rightText: and said unto them, We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to one that is uncircumcised; for that were a reproach unto us.

units.leftText: Only on this condition will we consent to you. If you will be as we are, that every male of you be circumcised,
units.rightText: Only on this condition will we consent unto you: if ye will be as we are, that every male of you be circumcised;

units.leftText: then will we give our daughters to you; and we will take your daughters to us, and we will dwell with you, and we will become one people.
units.rightText: then will we give our daughters unto you, and we will take your daughters to us, and we will dwell with you, and we will become one people.

units.leftText: But if you will not listen to us and be circumcised, then we will take our sister, and we will be gone.”
units.rightText: But if ye will not hearken unto us, to be circumcised; then will we take our daughter, and we will be gone.

units.leftText: Their words pleased Hamor and Shechem, Hamor’s son.
units.rightText: And their words pleased Hamor, and Shechem Hamor’s son.

units.leftText: The young man didn’t wait to do this thing, because he had delight in Jacob’s daughter, and he was honored above all the house of his father.
units.rightText: And the young man deferred not to do the thing, because he had delight in Jacob’s daughter: and he was honored above all the house of his father.

units.leftText: Hamor and Shechem, his son, came to the gate of their city, and talked with the men of their city, saying,
units.rightText: And Hamor and Shechem his son came unto the gate of their city, and communed with the men of their city, saying,

units.leftText: “These men are peaceful with us. Therefore let them live in the land and trade in it. For behold, the land is large enough for them. Let’s take their daughters to us for wives, and let’s give them our daughters.
units.rightText: These men are peaceable with us; therefore let them dwell in the land, and trade therein; for, behold, the land is large enough for them; let us take their daughters to us for wives, and let us give them our daughters.

units.leftText: Only on this condition will the men consent to us to live with us, to become one people, if every male among us is circumcised, as they are circumcised.
units.rightText: Only on this condition will the men consent unto us to dwell with us, to become one people, if every male among us be circumcised, as they are circumcised.

units.leftText: Won’t their livestock and their possessions and all their animals be ours? Only let’s give our consent to them, and they will dwell with us.”
units.rightText: Shall not their cattle and their substance and all their beasts be ours? only let us consent unto them, and they will dwell with us.

units.leftText: All who went out of the gate of his city listened to Hamor, and to Shechem his son; and every male was circumcised, all who went out of the gate of his city.
units.rightText: And unto Hamor and unto Shechem his son hearkened all that went out of the gate of his city; and every male was circumcised, all that went out of the gate of his city.

units.leftText: On the third day, when they were sore, two of Jacob’s sons, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers, each took his sword, came upon the unsuspecting city, and killed all the males.
units.rightText: And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city unawares, and slew all the males.

units.leftText: They killed Hamor and Shechem, his son, with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechem’s house, and went away.
units.rightText: And they slew Hamor and Shechem his son with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechem’s house, and went forth.

units.leftText: Jacob’s sons came on the dead, and plundered the city, because they had defiled their sister.
units.rightText: The sons of Jacob came upon the slain, and plundered the city, because they had defiled their sister.

units.leftText: They took their flocks, their herds, their donkeys, that which was in the city, that which was in the field,
units.rightText: They took their flocks and their herds and their asses, and that which was in the city, and that which was in the field;

units.leftText: and all their wealth. They took captive all their little ones and their wives, and took as plunder everything that was in the house.
units.rightText: and all their wealth, and all their little ones and their wives, took they captive and made a prey, even all that was in the house.

units.leftText: Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “You have troubled me, to make me odious to the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites. I am few in number. They will gather themselves together against me and strike me, and I will be destroyed, I and my house.”
units.rightText: And Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, Ye have troubled me, to make me odious to the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites: and, I being few in number, they will gather themselves together against me and smite me; and I shall be destroyed, I and my house.

units.leftText: They said, “Should he deal with our sister as with a prostitute?”
units.rightText: And they said, Should he deal with our sister as with a harlot?

units.leftText: God said to Jacob, “Arise, go up to Bethel, and live there. Make there an altar to God, who appeared to you when you fled from the face of Esau your brother.”
units.rightText: And God said unto Jacob, Arise, go up to Beth-el, and dwell there: and make there an altar unto God, who appeared unto thee when thou fleddest from the face of Esau thy brother.

units.leftText: Then Jacob said to his household, and to all who were with him, “Put away the foreign gods that are among you, purify yourselves, and change your garments.
units.rightText: Then Jacob said unto his household, and to all that were with him, Put away the foreign gods that are among you, and purify yourselves, and change your garments:

units.leftText: Let’s arise, and go up to Bethel. I will make there an altar to God, who answered me in the day of my distress, and was with me on the way which I went.”
units.rightText: and let us arise, and go up to Beth-el; and I will make there an altar unto God, who answered me in the day of my distress, and was with me in the way which I went.

units.leftText: They gave to Jacob all the foreign gods which were in their hands, and the rings which were in their ears; and Jacob hid them under the oak which was by Shechem.
units.rightText: And they gave unto Jacob all the foreign gods which were in their hand, and the rings which were in their ears; and Jacob hid them under the oak which was by Shechem.

units.leftText: They traveled, and a terror of God was on the cities that were around them, and they didn’t pursue the sons of Jacob.
units.rightText: And they journeyed: and a terror of God was upon the cities that were round about them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.

units.leftText: So Jacob came to Luz (that is, Bethel), which is in the land of Canaan, he and all the people who were with him.
units.rightText: So Jacob came to Luz, which is in the land of Canaan (the same is Beth-el), he and all the people that were with him.

units.leftText: He built an altar there, and called the place El Beth El; because there God was revealed to him, when he fled from the face of his brother.
units.rightText: And he built there an altar, and called the place El-beth-el; because there God was revealed unto him, when he fled from the face of his brother.

units.leftText: Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, died, and she was buried below Bethel under the oak; and its name was called Allon Bacuth.
units.rightText: And Deborah Rebekah’s nurse died, and she was buried below Beth-el under the oak: and the name of it was called Allon-bacuth.

units.leftText: God appeared to Jacob again, when he came from Paddan Aram, and blessed him.
units.rightText: And God appeared unto Jacob again, when he came from Paddan-aram, and blessed him.

units.leftText: God said to him, “Your name is Jacob. Your name shall not be Jacob any more, but your name will be Israel.” He named him Israel.
units.rightText: And God said unto him, Thy name is Jacob: thy name shall not be called any more Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name: and he called his name Israel.

units.leftText: God said to him, “I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and multiply. A nation and a company of nations will be from you, and kings will come out of your body.
units.rightText: And God said unto him, I am God Almighty: be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee, and kings shall come out of thy loins;

units.leftText: The land which I gave to Abraham and Isaac, I will give it to you, and to your offspring after you I will give the land.”
units.rightText: and the land which I gave unto Abraham and Isaac, to thee I will give it, and to thy seed after thee will I give the land.

units.leftText: God went up from him in the place where he spoke with him.
units.rightText: And God went up from him in the place where he spake with him.

units.leftText: Jacob set up a pillar in the place where he spoke with him, a pillar of stone. He poured out a drink offering on it, and poured oil on it.
units.rightText: And Jacob set up a pillar in the place where he spake with him, a pillar of stone: and he poured out a drink-offering thereon, and poured oil thereon.

units.leftText: Jacob called the name of the place where God spoke with him “Bethel”.
units.rightText: And Jacob called the name of the place where God spake with him, Beth-el.

units.leftText: They traveled from Bethel. There was still some distance to come to Ephrath, and Rachel travailed. She had hard labor.
units.rightText: And they journeyed from Beth-el; and there was still some distance to come to Ephrath: and Rachel travailed, and she had hard labor.

units.leftText: When she was in hard labor, the midwife said to her, “Don’t be afraid, for now you will have another son.”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when she was in hard labor, that the midwife said unto her, Fear not; for now thou shalt have another son.

units.leftText: As her soul was departing (for she died), she named him Benoni, but his father named him Benjamin.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as her soul was departing (for she died), that she called his name Ben-oni: but his father called him Benjamin.

units.leftText: Rachel died, and was buried on the way to Ephrath (also called Bethlehem).
units.rightText: And Rachel died, and was buried in the way to Ephrath (the same is Beth-lehem).

units.leftText: Jacob set up a pillar on her grave. The same is the Pillar of Rachel’s grave to this day.
units.rightText: And Jacob set up a pillar upon her grave: the same is the Pillar of Rachel’s grave unto this day.

units.leftText: Israel traveled, and spread his tent beyond the tower of Eder.
units.rightText: And Israel journeyed, and spread his tent beyond the tower of Eder.

units.leftText: While Israel lived in that land, Reuben went and lay with Bilhah, his father’s concubine, and Israel heard of it.

units.rightText: Now these are the generations of Esau (the same is Edom).

units.leftText: For their substance was too great for them to dwell together, and the land of their travels couldn’t bear them because of their livestock.
